source_row.rationale: IV promethazine carries a well-documented risk of severe tissue injury, including necrosis and gangrene, particularly if the medication extravasates into surrounding tissue or is inadvertently administered intra-arterially. Given this significant risk, FDA warnings and safety guidance recommend extreme caution with IV administration, and many institutions have shifted toward preferring alternative routes or highly diluted, slow administration through a well-functioning, larger vein when IV use is necessary.
